text_en:
Maintenance Procedure Information System
 | Protection | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: OCR-087-r0a | Equipment:
 Overcurrent and Earth Leakage Protection
 MIF II 
 GE
Issued to: 
 Distribution Companies
Status: 
 Draft
Approval date: 
 2009 | Procedure:
 Single-phase secondary current injection device ('Ampere')
Next review date: 
 2014
Introduction
This document sets out the steps to be followed when testing the overcurrent and earth leakage protection device, model MIF II.
This document was prepared by Alexandria Electricity Distribution Company and was reviewed and approved by the MPIS coordinators.
Safety Precautions
Notify the competent control/operation of the cells on which the protection is to be tested. | 
Issue an approved work order specifying the work location and the work team, observing occupational safety and health rules. | 
The work team must carry the occupational safety and health category card. | 
Ensure the cell circuit breaker is switched off by the competent operation technician and the circuit breaker placed in the test position. | 
Ensure warning signs are posted on the cells to be worked on. | 
Ensure the protection device is earthed. | 
Observe polarity when dealing with DC voltage.
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Single-phase secondary injection device ('Ampere'). | 
Three Phase Circuit Analyzer device. | 
Load clamp and avometer. | 
Suitable laptop computer with the relay software. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
First: Testing the Non-Directional Overcurrent Characteristic (measured values are compared with rated values)
Ensure the DC auxiliary voltage is present on the protection device at points A1 +ve, A2 -ve as in the figure. | 
Prepare the injection device and supply it with the appropriate AC auxiliary voltage for operation | 2.
Place the current leads on the protection device at points R = C1-C2 | 3.
Raise the current gradually until reaching the pickup current of the protection device and record this value | 4.
Lower the current gradually until reaching the I Reset current of the protection device and record this value | 5.
Calculate the reset factor K (Reset factors) = Ireset / I pick up > 95% | 6.
Repeat these steps for the second and third phases | 7.
Connect the Trip leads of the device to the Stop Timer terminals of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 8.
Ensure the tripping signal of the protection device is received at the control centre | 9.
Testing the Instantaneous Short-Circuit Currents Characteristic
Raise the current gradually until reaching the operating current set on the device | 1.
Repeat these steps for the second and third phases | 2.
Connect the Trip leads of the device to the Stop timer terminal of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 3.
Second: Testing the Non-Directional Earth Leakage Characteristic
Connect the current leads to the protection device at points C7, C8 | 1.
Raise the current gradually until reaching the pickup current I pick up of the protection device and record this value | 2.
Lower the current gradually until reaching the I reset current of the protection device and record this value | 3.
Calculate the reset factor K reset factor = Ireset / Ipick up > 95% | 4.
Connect the Trip leads of the device to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 5.
Ensure the tripping signal of the protection device is received at the control centre | 
Testing the Instantaneous Short-Circuit Currents Characteristic
Raise the current gradually until reaching the operating current set on the device | 1.
Connect the Trip leads of the device to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 2.
